title: Next-Installment Pull on a Past-Due Patient Payment Plan
content:
**Desk guidance — the coming installment in a Patient Payment Plan catch-up**

A next-installment pull adds part of the coming installment: where at least 25 calendar days have passed since the due date of the latest missed installment, counting that due date as day zero, and a returned-payment fee was booked on that installment, the whole coming installment is added; where that many days have passed and no returned-payment fee was booked on it, 0.5 of an installment is added; where fewer days have passed nothing is added. The amount added is that part of the installment in force.

The pulled amount, being above what the missed installments call for, is applied as the tier's handling of an amount above what is due provides — to principal, reducing the balance, on every tier of the Patient Payment Plan — and the coming installment is still collected on its own due date.

## Input, judgement, result

| Calendar days since the latest missed installment's due date | Returned-payment fee booked on that installment | Added to the catch-up |
|---|---|---|
| 25 or more | Yes | The whole installment in force |
| 25 or more | No | 0.5 of the installment in force |
| 24 or fewer | Either | Nothing |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, latest missed installment due 2026-05-01, installment in force 140.00)

- Handled 2026-05-25 (day 24): nothing is added.
- Handled 2026-05-26 (day 25), with a returned-payment fee on the 2026-05-01 installment: 140.00 is added.
- Handled 2026-05-26 (day 25), with no returned-payment fee on it: 70.00 is added.
